 Order

The petitioners are the accused Nos.1 to 3 in Crime No.786/2025 of Puthencruz Police Station,
Ernakulam, a Crime registered in respect of the offences under Sections 406, 420, 506, 34, 35, 37 and 120B of IPC, as per the directions of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kolencherry,
under Section 175(3) BNSS in a complaint filed by the 2nd respondent.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kolencherry
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The crux of the allegations against the petitioners is that they failed to make payment of the balance sale consideration of Rs.35 lakhs to the de facto complainant/2nd respondent, from whom the petitioners purchased a residential house along with landed property having an extent of 6.75 cents.
It is stated that the property was agreed to be purchased for a sale consideration of Rs.95 lakhs, out of which only Rs.60 lakhs were paid by the petitioners.
The de facto complainant would further allege that the petitioners resorted to threatening her and her son, whenever they demanded the payment of balance sale consideration.

3. A complaint which the 2nd respondent preferred before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kolencherry, in the above regard, was 2025:KER:74142       forwarded to the SHO of Police, Puthencruz, under Section 175(3) BNSS.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kolencherry
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the case has been registered and the investigation commenced.

4. In the present petition, the petitioners would contend that none of the offences as alleged by the de facto complainant are attracted even if the entire allegations in her complaint are accepted as such.
It is further stated that the remedy which the de facto complaint could avail is under the civil law, and not to resort to criminal prosecution for cheating and criminal breach of trust.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned counsel for the de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

sentences.text: 6. Annexure A2 is the complaint which the 2nd respondent filed before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kolencherry, against the petitioners herein alleging the commission of the aforesaid offences.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kolencherry
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A reading of the aforesaid complaint would reveal that the issue pertains to the failure of the petitioners to make payment of the balance sale consideration for the house and property which they purchased from the de facto complainant.

There is absolutely nothing in the aforesaid complaint which would show that right from the very beginning, when the petitioners entered into the agreement with the de facto complainant for the purchase of her property, the petitioners fraudulently and dishonestly intended to avoid payment of the balance sale consideration.

In that view of the matter, it is not possible to say that the allegations in Annexure A2 complaint which resulted in the registration of this Crime, would constitute the offence of cheating as envisaged under Section 420 IPC.
So also, it is not possible to say that the transaction as revealed from Annexure A2 would attract the ingredients of criminal breach of trust as envisaged under Section 406 IPC.

As regards the allegation of criminal intimidation, it is seen from para 4 of the Annexure A2 complaint that there is only a vague statement to the effect that the 1st petitioner had called the son of the de facto complainant and threatened him over telephone.
The nature of the criminal intimidation or the precise words of threatening alleged to be committed by the 1st petitioner are not disclosed in the aforesaid complaint.
It is thus not possible to say that the aforesaid allegation would attract the ingredients of Section 506 IPC.
Likewise, there is absolutely nothing on record to show that the accused 2025:KER:74142       hatched a criminal conspiracy for the commission of any of the aforesaid offences.
Therefore, there is substance in the contention of the petitioners that the criminal prosecution has been launched against them without any basis.

8. Time and again, the Hon'ble Apex Court has warned the authorities concerned against entertaining false criminal complaints preferred by unscrupulous litigants, and their attempt to give the colour of criminal liability to civil issues.
The present case appears to be one of that nature.
Therefore, the prayer of the petitioners to quash the criminal prosecution initiated against them is fully justified.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.

Annexure A1 FIR registered by the Puthencruz Police in Crime No.786/2025, and all proceedings initiated against the petitioners pursuant to the registration of the aforesaid Crime, are hereby quashed.
